name: Can I live in my older home during a renovation?

mainEntity.name: Can I live in my older home during a renovation?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can often remain in part of an older home during renovation, but it depends on dust, utility outages, access, structural work, and the number of rooms affected. Context: kitchens, bathrooms, additions, and whole-home projects can interrupt water, power, cooking, bathing, or circulation. Key factors: children or pets, lead or asbestos concerns, temporary facilities, work-zone separation, and the project sequence. Practical guidance: ask for an occupancy plan identifying protected areas, shutdowns, daily cleanup, and a backup arrangement for essential utilities. Remove valuables and fragile belongings before demolition. A phased scope may reduce disruption but can extend the overall project.
acceptedAnswer.description: Sometimes, but the decision depends on dust, hazardous-material concerns, utility shutdowns, structural work, access, and how many rooms are affected. Ask for an occupancy and containment plan, including temporary kitchen or bathroom arrangements and expected shutdowns.
